column2: “That's what I'm saying!{r}{p}
We just got back to our room, and on the floor there was this... this...!”
The girls, trembling, held out a small scrap of paper to Mr. Kobayashi.
Peeking in from the side, I saw characters scrawled with something like a red marker.
“Tonight
the kamaitachi
will appear”
“Kamaitachi...
what could that mean?”
Saying so, I turned around,
and {n2} was staring at the scrap of paper with a deathly pale face.
What's wrong?”
{n2} gasped and shook her head.
“Huh?
...No, it's nothing.”
Something was clearly wrong.
{n2}'s face was still drained of color.
But
I didn't press her.
I started thinking alone about the “kamaitachi.”
Kamaitachi...
I had heard the word.
If I remembered right, it was a phenomenon where a whirlwind or something created a vacuum and caused cuts.
People in the old days apparently blamed it on a weasel-like animal carrying a sickle.
But what could it mean that this kamaitachi
“tonight
will appear”?
Was it something like a weather forecast?
Something like
“Today, cloudy then snow, with kamaitachi in some areas”...?
Surely not.
I couldn't believe it.
I had never heard of anything like that.
“I wonder what it means.”
Mr. Kobayashi murmured to no one in particular.
“I don't know, but...
it's kind of creepy, isn't it?”
Keiko said, seeking agreement, and the other two nodded along.
“Either someone's prank, or if not...
“If not?”
When I asked about his hesitation, he glanced at me and said quietly:
“Maybe someone got the wrong room.”
“The wrong room?”
“Yes.
It might be a message meant for somebody else.”
“Somebody else?”
“The room next door or across the hall, I can't say...
that person might understand its meaning.{r}{p}Well, either way, I don't think you need to worry about it.”
Mr. Kobayashi turned to the girls and said so with a shrug.
If I hadn't seen {n2}'s pale face, I could have brushed it off that easily too.
But...
When I looked at {n2}, she turned her face away smoothly as if nothing had happened.
“Oh,
I just remembered something I need to do.{r}{p}I'm going up to my room, so you can wait in the lounge or something, {n1}.”
okay.”
Barely waiting for my answer, {n2} vanished up the stairs to the second floor like the wind.
Luckily, nobody else seemed to notice {n2}'s odd behavior.
As I drifted away from the front desk to follow {n2}, Mr. Kobayashi called out to me.
Care for a drink?{r}{p}Coffee or tea...
or a beer, if you like.”
sure.”
It seemed odd to refuse, so I ended up nodding.
“How about you ladies?
It's on the house.”
Mr. Kobayashi said to the girls.
They exchanged looks, nodded enthusiastically, and answered.
“Yes, please!”
To them, the suspicious note no longer seemed to matter at all.
But for me, that wasn't the case.
{n2}'s attitude bothered me.
Sitting on the lounge sofa, I thought about the author of the note.
Who had written it, and for whom?
Who exactly was staying near their rooms?
Should I ask these girls?
I looked at the three faces.
And then...
I decided to ask Kanako.
“Hey,
do you know who's staying near your room?”
“Near us?
...Hmm, no idea.{r}{p}I wasn't paying attention.{r}{p}Aki, do you know?”
“Near us?{r}{p}Hmm, if I remember right, the room across from us is hers? {n2}, was it?{r}{p}I saw her going in and out.”
{n2} is in the room across...
Hearing that only increased my anxiety.
The real addressee of that message might have been {n2}.
If so, it wouldn't be strange if she could understand the meaning hidden in the message.
and next door?”
I pulled myself together and asked further.
“Next door?
Hmm...”
I decided to wait for Mr. Kobayashi, who had stepped into the back, to come out.
For this kind of thing, asking the inn's owner is the surest.
Before long he came back with a tray, together with his wife, Kyoko.
But just as I was about to speak up, {n2} came down from the second floor.
...In the end, I still knew nothing.
{n2} sat down next to me, smiling brightly as if nothing had happened.
“You'll have tea too, won't you, {n2}?”
Kyoko asked, and {n2} nodded with a bright smile.
She looked exactly like her usual self.
The expression earlier must have been my imagination.
Or maybe she had just been feeling unwell.
In any case, {n2} had nothing to do with that note.
I forced myself to think so.
Just then, a light like headlights flickered through the falling snow outside the dark window.
“Huh?
Someone's arriving at this hour?”
I murmured, and Mr. Kobayashi turned to the window too.
“Probably that Mikimoto fellow.{r}{p}He called to say he'd be late.”
We heard a car stop out back, and before long the door opened and a big man burst in with the blizzard.
“Whew, thank goodness!”
“Welcome.
Are you Mr. Mikimoto?”
Mr. Kobayashi called out.
“That's me, that's me!
Boy, what a time I've had.”
He'd come by car, so he should only have walked the distance from the parking lot, but snow had already piled up on his shoulders and head.
Slapping off the snow, the man called Mikimoto took off his shoes and headed for the front desk.
“I'm afraid dinner is already over, but if you like, I could prepare some onigiri or something.”
“Onigiri?
Wonderful!{r}{p}I was about to starve to death.”
“I see.
Then once you've changed, please come to the dining room or the lounge there.”
Mr. Mikimoto finished signing in and carried his big luggage up to the second floor.
“Doesn't look like the skiing type.{r}{p}Maybe he climbs snowy mountains.”
{n2} whispered on the sly.
“Right.”
He was indeed big, his face full of beard, the very picture of a mountain man.
Glancing at the girls, I saw them glaring sharply at the stairs.
But the moment they noticed my gaze, they hurriedly lowered their eyes and went back to trivial chatter.
“Hey, hey,
did you see last night's?{r}{p}'Analects'!”
I hadn't seen it, but I think the full title was 'Nothing But the Analects, Right?', a trendy philosophy drama.
“I saw it, I saw it!
What a shock!{r}{p}Mencius confessing to Confucius...”
“I was more surprised that Laozi showed up when I thought he didn't exist.”
I wondered what on earth the story was.
“The tea is ready.”
Kyoko set cups before everyone and poured apple-scented tea.
The part-timers Midori and Toshio had apparently caught the scent and came from the dining room.
“Would you two like some?”
At Kyoko's words, both nodded as if they'd been waiting.
Just then Mr. Mikimoto came down, and on cue Mr. Kobayashi returned with the onigiri.
Suddenly the lounge was full of people, lively with all sorts of idle chatter.
“The love triangle with Laozi...”
“So when you're doing parallel, you put the foot on the mountain side...”
“This is delicious rice, isn't it?{r}{p}{g}
I wonder where it's from...
That's how it went.
Mr. and Mrs. Kobayashi, of course, and Toshio and Midori too, were all kind, fun people.
Just being there with {n2}, I was able to have a very pleasant time.
When I noticed, it was already past ten at night.
My body was exhausted, and I had to be ready for tomorrow.
Everyone seemed to think the same, and when {n2} and I stood up, the modest gathering broke up.
“Good night.”
“Please teach me parallel tomorrow, okay?”
“Get some good rest.”
Everyone filed up the stairs toward their own rooms.
{n2} was heading briskly back to her room, looking distracted.
Should I invite her to my room, or not...
Ah,
the door would close if I didn't hurry.
After agonizing, I...
Wait up!”
I called out from behind.
“What?”
{n2} turned around looking annoyed.
wanna come
to my room?”
“To your room?
Why?”
She asked back, puzzled.
“Why? Well...
to talk,
or play games...”
“In other words, you don't have any particular reason.”
{n2} said it as if angry.
“Well, yeah, I guess so...”
“Sorry.
I feel a bit unwell and I'm not in the mood.{r}{p}Good night.”
More than unwell, she seemed unable to stop worrying about something.
Was it that note on her mind?
Did {n2} have something to do with that note after all?
Back in my room, I took a shower hoping to wash away my anxiety along with the sweat, but it did no good.
Even in bed I kept worrying about {n2} and tossed and turned.
Still, while listening quietly to the wind howling in the darkness, I gradually grew drowsy.
...Just as I was dozing off, there was a knock.
My drowsiness vanished in an instant.
{n2} had sneaked to my room!
I leaped out of bed, dashed to the door, and flung it open.
Backlit by the hallway light, a voluptuous silhouette emerged.
“Hey,
wanna drink?”
She said, a bottle of something in one hand.
I gulped and turned on the room light.
It wasn't {n2}.
By the time I realized it, she had already walked into the room.
Wata...
Ms. Watase?”
“Call me Kanako.”
Whispering it in my ear, her body smelled of fresh shampoo and soap.
“Wh-wh-wh...
why?”
I was hopelessly confused.
“Mind if I sit?”
Without waiting for an answer, she sat on the bed where I'd just been sleeping.
Where she'd gotten it, I don't know, but what she held was a wine bottle.
And in her other hand, two wine glasses, thoughtfully prepared.
I had no choice but to accept the glass she held out.
Red wine, filled to the brim.
“To a lovely encounter.”
The touching glasses made an alluring sound.
A lovely encounter...
Was she talking about her and me?
“Come on...”
She set the bottle on the floor and pulled my arm to seat me beside her.
Glancing over, I could see her cleavage through her deeply cut collar.
leaned my face closer to see better.
She didn't seem to be wearing a bra.
Which means those two bumps showing through this top{@}
are...!
Gulp...
I swallowed.
Damn, she might have heard that.
“Want to...
see more?”
“Want to...
see more?”
“N-no, not really...”
Looking away, I gulped down the wine in one go.
“You can really hold it.”
She whispered as if blowing her breath into my ear.
Could this be...
Was she, by any chance,
trying to seduce me...?
“That girl {n2},
do you like her?”
Out of nowhere, she asked that.
“Huh?{r}{p}...Well,
yeah,
kind of.”
“But she still won't let you do a thing, right?”
She said something terrifying so casually.
“You should just give up on a stuck-up girl like that.”
Saying so, she gazed at me with moist eyes.
Somehow I started to feel strangely floaty, like I was walking on clouds.
Looking at her again, I realized she was so attractive that {n2} couldn't even compare.
She gently took my hand and placed it on her knee.
let me make you feel good,
just
for
you.”
Her voice rang like heavenly music, and that alone nearly made me faint.
I flung the empty glass to the floor and pushed Kanako down onto the bed...
...I was flying through the sky.
Through the clear blue sky, {n2} and I flew gazing at each other...
...No, it's not {n2}, it's Kanako...
Or is it {n2} after all?
Whichever, I don't care...
“Get a grip...
Get a grip!”
It was {n2}'s voice, all right.
you're wonderful...”
“Idiot!
What are you saying?!”
There was a slap, and pain shot through my cheek.
Opening my eyes faintly, I vaguely saw {n2} peering down at me.
Huh?
When did I fall asleep?
“Wake up!
Please, hurry!”
Sensing something dire in her voice, I mustered every ounce of will and forced my eyes open.
{n2} stood beside the bed, her face deathly pale.
Little by little, I began to remember what had happened.
I sat up with a start, looked around the room, and saw something unbelievable.
Kanako.
She seemed to be sitting slumped against the wall, but another mouth gaped open in her throat.
Her throat had been slashed straight across, and her chest was soaked in bright red blood.
ah-ah-ah...”
I sucked in a breath, my mouth opening and closing.
I couldn't tell whether I was trying to say something or just trying to breathe.
sh...
She's dead!”
“Keep your voice down!”
{n2} pressed a finger to my lips.
but...
she...”
“You didn't do it, did you?”
I was stunned.
M-
M-m-me...?
Me?
Of course I didn't do that!”
“Then why is she here?”
She grilled me with an accusing stare.
“I didn't do anything...
She just showed up out of nowhere...
and said let's drink together...”
The more I remembered, the smaller my voice got.
“A honey trap, then.”
She said the strangest thing.
“A honey...
trap?{r}{p}What do you mean?”
She ignored my question and walked over to the body.
I peered at the body from behind {n2} too.
Her face was twisted hideously with fear and shock, with nothing left of how she'd looked in life.
Fighting back nausea, I looked away.
I couldn't believe {n2} was calmly examining the corpse's clothes and wound.
Suddenly I noticed something like bloody writing on the floor near the corpse's dangling arm.
Look at this!”
It clearly spelled out a word.
“Kamaitachi...!”
It had to be a message she wrote in her own blood in the moments before death, after her throat was cut.
A dying message, as they call it.
But for it to be “kamaitachi”...
What on earth did that mean?
Had the kamaitachi phenomenon really occurred just as the note predicted, and was that how her throat got cut?
“That can't be...”
{n2} cried out in surprise, as if she had read my mind.
“Right.
No matter what, a kamaitachi can't cut a person's throat.”
If something like that could happen, I might have been the one getting cut.
The thought made me shudder.
But {n2} was looking at me with a puzzled face.
Didn't she understand what I meant?
“What are you talking about?
Obviously somebody did this.{r}{p}This is murder.”
I know that.{r}{p}I do know.{r}{p}But 'kamaitachi'...”
“Don't worry about that.
It's irrelevant.”
{n2} brushed it aside flatly.
“Irrelevant...?
But the note said...
“That's not the issue right now!{r}{p}Someone...
someone in this inn killed her!”
{n2} cut off my words impatiently.
“Well, sure, but...”
“We have to tell Uncle.”
{n2} stood up.
“You stay here, {n1}.
Don't let anyone in.”
Strange...
Was {n2} used to situations like this?
Still, though her manner struck me as suspicious, all I could do was nod.
{n2} quietly opened the door.
She checked the hallway and slipped out without a sound.
Five minutes of waiting.
Mr. Kobayashi, who came back with {n2}, wore a stern look I had never seen before.
He silently entered the room and stood looking down at the body for a while.
When I started to speak, Mr. Kobayashi put a finger to his lips.
Apparently I wasn't supposed to talk.
He looked around the room once more, then suddenly got down on all fours like a dog and began peering under the bed and the side table.
Before long he reached under the bed.
When he stood up, between his fingertips was a small black object like a tiny cockroach.
He went to the window,{g}
threw it open, flung the object out, and shut the window fast.
What was that...?
I closed my mouth before I could ask.
Mr. Kobayashi was still searching for something.
He found the wine bottle on the floor, picked it up, and sniffed it.
He picked up the fallen glass, poured a little, swirled it, sniffed again, and tasted just a drop.
“Sleeping pills?”
{n2} asked in a low voice.
“No,
probably some kind of truth serum.”
“Truth serum?”
I let out a startled yelp.
I had heard of such a thing somewhere.
Instead of torture or whatever, they inject it to extract important information...
But why would anyone make me drink something like that?
“Don't shout.{r}{p}...So, Uncle, who do you think she was?”
“Who knows.”
Mr. Kobayashi said, checking the wine label.
“Top-grade Burgundy, and a vintage year at that.{r}{p}...Definitely the SDECE crowd.{r}{p}Anyone else wouldn't fuss over details like this.”
“What did you say...
The SDE...?”
When I asked back, {n2} answered in a tone that said, it's common knowledge.
“French intelligence.”
French intelligence?!”
I was so shocked I shouted out loud.
“Shh!”
{n2} and Mr. Kobayashi put fingers to their lips at the same time.
“What about that 'bug' from before?”
{n2} asked Mr. Kobayashi.
“Everyone would use a Japanese-made one anyway, wouldn't they?{r}{p}Besides, we don't know whether she planted that bug or whoever killed her did.”
I swallowed hard, then spoke in a whisper.
“What kind of joke is this?{r}{p}French intelligence, bugs, and...”
Even as I said it, one look at {n2} and Mr. Kobayashi told me this was no joke.
Mr. Kobayashi looked back and forth between me and {n2} for a while, then began to speak as if he had made up his mind.
“...Now that it's come to this, I suppose we'd better tell you too.”
{n2} looked displeased but shrugged in resignation.
“I guess we have no choice.”
“Y-you're not going to tell me
{n2}'s some kind of spy too, are you?”
I said it with a twitching smile.
“...'Spy' isn't the right word.{r}{p}Our main mission is to monitor other countries' intelligence activities inside Japan.
...Do you know?
That this country is called a spy paradise?”
“A spy paradise?”
“That's right.
You kids may think spies and intelligence agencies are stories from some far-off country, or fiction from the movies.{r}{p}Nothing to do with you.{r}{p}But that is a big mistake.”
“Japan has virtually no laws or systems restricting espionage.{r}{p}So there's no place in the world where they can operate as easily as here.”
I see.
So that's why it's a spy paradise...
“People who smuggle export-controlled computer hardware and software overseas to sell...{r}{p}Add in things like industrial espionage, and it's no exaggeration to say Japan is crawling with spies.
{r}{p}It's by no means someone else's problem.”
“But...
but I'm just a college
student!”
“She didn't seem to think so.”
Mr. Kobayashi said, indicating the body with his eyes.
“She didn't think so...
then what did she think I was?”
Mr. Kobayashi didn't answer right away.
I opened my mouth to ask again, and Mr. Kobayashi spoke.
“Maybe the Kamaitachi...
That's probably what she figured.”
I couldn't grasp the meaning of those words at once, and stayed confused for a while.
“Wait a second... {p}The Kamaitachi?
Then the kamaitachi is...?”
It was {n2} who answered.
“Right.
It's neither a monster nor a natural phenomenon.{r}{p}It's the code name of a legendary Eastern Bloc spy, whispered about more and more over the past ten years or so.”
“An Eastern Bloc spy?
But the Soviet Union doesn't exist anymore...”
“That's exactly the problem.”
What a slow one,
her look seemed to say.
“With the Soviets and nearly the whole Eastern Bloc collapsed, the 'Kamaitachi' has lost its employer.{r}{p}So what options does he, or she, have left?”
I thought a moment and gave a random answer.
“Change careers?”
“What could a spy possibly turn into at this point?{r}{p}No.
Find a new employer.”
“A new employer...”
I still didn't quite get it.
“Listen.
The 'Kamaitachi,' who worked for the East for so long,

must still hold a huge amount of vital information, even now that US-Soviet tensions have eased.{r}{p}Some of it surely includes major secrets about the Self-Defense Forces and US forces in Japan.{r}{p}There are plenty of countries that would pay
any fortune to get that information.”
“And conversely, if some other country seizes that information, it would be a major blow to both Japan and America.{r}{p}If possible, we want the 'Kamaitachi' on our side.
Even if that fails, we must at least stop the information from falling into someone else's hands.”
It was an absurdly unreal story.
{n2}, who was supposed to be an ordinary cute college girl...
It didn't sound like something that could come out of her mouth.
But if you put it that way, the corpse in front of me was just as far removed from my everyday life.
I had no choice but to believe {n2}'s words.
Still, many questions remained.
“So you thought I might be that 'Kamaitachi'?{r}{p}Why on earth?{r}{p}There can't be spies in a mountain place like this!”
{n2} glanced at Mr. Kobayashi.
This time Mr. Kobayashi began to speak.
in fact it seems fairly certain that the 'Kamaitachi' really would show up here tonight.{r}{p}You saw it too,
the note those office ladies brought.”
I remembered.
The kamaitachi will appear tonight...
Once you understood, the note meant exactly what it said.

“We had also independently learned that the 'Kamaitachi' would soon make contact with some country's intelligence service at this inn.{r}{p}Luckily we had time to spare, so we got the owner's cooperation
and set up this trap.”
“Then Mr. Kobayashi isn't really the owner...
“Of course not.
The real owner is probably enjoying a trip abroad about now.”
“So being {n2}'s uncle was a lie too?”
Belatedly realizing I'd been fooled, I started getting angry.
{n2} answered, seemingly oblivious to my feelings.
“Sort of.
But he's a distant relative, so it's not a total lie.”
“Then why...
why on earth did you invite me to a place like this?”
Had I just imagined that she felt even a little fondness for me?
Perhaps {n2} found it too hard to answer, because Mr. Kobayashi spoke instead.
“...For camouflage.{r}{p}A young couple is less likely to arouse suspicion.{r}{p}Of course, we had young male members too, but...{r}{p}To fool the eyes of a seasoned professional,
we concluded the best choice was a perfectly ordinary student who knew nothing at all.”
I had been invited skiing purely as camouflage...
Should I be sad, or should I be angry?
“Do you think those two are part of it too?”
{n2} seemed to mean the two remaining office ladies.
“...We'd better assume so.”
“Sh-
shouldn't we call the police?{r}{p}This is a murder!”
“Catching the 'Kamaitachi' comes first.{r}{p}If the police come now, he'll never show his true colors.”
“But isn't the 'Kamaitachi' the murderer?{r}{p}A proper investigation might catch him.”
“No, the 'Kamaitachi' isn't necessarily the culprit.{r}{p}The killer may have left that dying message on purpose.”
“Why would the killer need to do that?”
“Same as the note.{r}{p}To smoke out the 'Kamaitachi.'”
I didn't quite follow.
{n2} explained it for me.

“That note was probably written by those girls.{r}{p}They showed it around to see how everyone would react.{r}{p}I reacted.{r}{p}So they figured you, who were with me, must be one of us too, and approached you
to find out who you were.”
So that was it...
I finally understood.
“First things first, let's hide the body.”
Mr. Kobayashi said it as a matter of course, and {n2} nodded.
He stripped the sheet off the unused bed and spread it next to the body.
“What are you standing there for?{r}{p}Roll the body onto this.”
He said it irritably.
“Huh?
Really?”
“Who else?”
{n2} made no move to help.
With no choice, I approached the body and, together with Mr. Kobayashi,
rolled it onto the sheet.
A red stain spread across the pure white sheet before my eyes.
“All right, let's carry it to the bathroom.”
We wrapped the body in the sheet, and with me at the feet and Mr. Kobayashi at the head, we hid it in the bathroom.
“Hiding just the body won't help. The floor is soaked in blood.”
I said, my voice trembling.
“I know.”
Mr. Kobayashi answered, fetched a bath towel, and started wiping the floor.
But it wouldn't come completely clean.
Just when I thought so, after soaking up most of the blood, Mr. Kobayashi splashed wine all over the place.
The overpowering smell of wine masked the smell of blood quite well.
“That should fool them for a while.{r}{p}...Don't let anyone in until morning.”
Mr. Kobayashi glared at me and started to leave.
wait a minute! You mean I'm supposed to just...
sleep here like this? With that in there?”
I said, glancing at the bathroom door.
“It can't be helped.{r}{p}Act as if nothing happened.{r}{p}Even if her friends come looking, play dumb and stick to it.”
I started to protest that I could never sleep in a room with a corpse, but Mr. Kobayashi wouldn't listen and quietly left the room.
Holding a faint hope, I looked at {n2}, who remained.
{n2} smiled apologetically.
“Sorry.
Just bear with it for one night.{r}{p}...Well, good night.”
Heartlessly, she left too.
I was left all alone with the body.
Even though it was in the bathroom and out of sight, there was no way I could sleep at a murder scene where bloodstains still remained.
I resolved to stay up all night and thought about some way to take my mind off it.
And so...
I got into bed, closed my eyes, and decided to count sheep.
I got into bed, closed my eyes, and decided to count sheep.
One sheep...
Two sheep...
Three sheep...
I pictured sheep leaping over a fence, one after another.
Whenever the bloody corpse came to mind, I desperately focused on the sheep.
One hundred twenty sheep...
One hundred twenty-one sheep...
One hundred twenty-two sheep...
...Was she really dead?
Could she come back to life?
I fought the urge to open my eyes and look at the bathroom door, and began counting sheep again.
Eight hundred ninety-three sheep...
Eight hundred ninety-four sheep...
Eight hundred ninety-five sheep...
Damn it,
I really can't sleep with the lights on.
But turning them off is scary too...
Dozing off now and then, I counted up to nine thousand two hundred fifteen sheep before I couldn't take it anymore and decided to go downstairs.
It was almost six in the morning.
The blizzard showed no sign of letting up, and the lounge, its lights off, was dimly lit.
Midori, coming out of the dining room, stopped short with a start.
“Oh, you scared me!
...You're up early.”
“Oh,
good morning.”
“Morning.
You couldn't sleep either, huh?”
Either?
As I wondered what “either” meant, she came closer and whispered in my ear.
“Don't worry.
The Boss told me.{r}{p}You got dragged into something strange, didn't you.”
Then she smiled reassuringly.
I see.
If they had persuaded the owner to swap places, then of course Toshio and Midori were Mr. Kobayashi's subordinates too.
That made me feel a little better.
“How about some coffee to wake you up?{r}{p}Breakfast is still a while off.”
I gratefully accepted.
She turned on the lights, and when I sat in the lounge and took a sip of hot coffee, it felt like the knots all over my body were melting away.
Tension and lack of sleep had apparently worn me out without my realizing it.
Sounds of breakfast preparations drifted from the dining room, and at six-thirty {n2} came down too.
“Good morning.
Did you sleep okay?”
As if nothing had happened, she greeted me with a bright smile.
I almost got angry, thinking how could I possibly have slept,
but...
I stopped when I saw the two office ladies coming down behind her.
“...Sort of.”
The office ladies showed no particular interest in me or {n2}.
Maybe they, like me, were genuine ordinary office workers invited as camouflage.
When {n2} sat down next to me, Aki Kawamura, the one with glasses, asked with a worried look.
excuse me, but
did you happen to see the girl with long hair who was with us?{r}{p}She wasn't there when I woke up.”
Did she know the girl came to my room, and was she testing my reaction?
She looked like a perfectly ordinary office worker worried about her friend, but was that an act too?
I couldn't know the truth, but I put on the best act I could.
“No,
I haven't seen her.”
As I said that and looked at {n2}, she shook her head too.
“I did meet her last night, though.”
I said, watching both their faces.
If they were part of it too, they surely knew she had come to my room, so I figured hiding it would be a mistake.
